content:
ana_support: FYI — customer reported intermittent 502s + spikes (p95 ~5-6s) on POST /v1/generate. They provided one request_id and a curl. Quoting their message:
> request_id: req_9f3b2a
> time: 2026-03-05T14:22:13Z
> curl: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"test"}'`

Can someone try a server log lookup and confirm whether the backend returned a 502 or we hit a timeout fallback?

sam_ops: I can check. Running internal log search: `ri logs search --request-id req_9f3b2a --env prod --start 2026-03-05T14:20:00Z --end 2026-03-05T14:25:00Z --fields timestamp,service,status,latency_ms,message`

sam_ops: results snippet:
```
2026-03-05T14:22:13Z | edge-gateway | 502 | 5120ms | upstream read timeout
2026-03-05T14:22:13Z | model-router | 502 | 5100ms | connection reset by peer
2026-03-05T14:22:12Z | edge-gateway | 200 | 120ms | health-check probe
```

sam_ops: So edge saw an upstream timeout and the model-router connection was reset. Looks like model-host side transient.

maya_infra: quick note on retention — hosted (free/standard) logs are retained for 7 days by default. If the timestamp the customer gave had been older than 7 days we would not find any entries and would need to escalate to log-archiver. For enterprise customers we keep 30d and can pull archived buckets on request.

ana_support: Customer is on standard hosted (not enterprise). The event is within 7d so we found it. Can we capture the debug bundle and share repro steps so they can reproduce? They included a simple curl but not the response headers (X-Request-Id or X-Correlation-Id). Ask them to re-run with `-i` and include response headers.

jordan_devx: Suggested repro curl (paste this to customer):
```
# run from customer's environment to capture response headers and timings
curl -i -w "\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code} TIME_TOTAL:%{time_total}s" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Debug: true" \
  -d '{"input":"<small test>"}'
```

jordan_devx: Also ask them to send back the full response (headers + body) and the exact time (UTC) they ran the curl. If they can include an `X-Request-Id` from the response that will make lookups deterministic.

ana_support: I'll ask for those and also generate a debug bundle token: `DebugBundleBot: create-bundle --ttl 72h --note "support case 4521"`.

DebugBundleBot: debug bundle created: https://internal.redwood/debug-bundles/DB-4521 (token expires in 72h). Include this link for the customer to upload their client-side capture if they want us to attach it.

maya_infra: From infra side, the model-host logs show a transient socket reset at 14:22:13Z. Hypothesis: short lived overload on that host during a rolling gc/oom event. I'll check host-level metrics (GPU utilisation, memory pressure) for that time window. If it's a recurring pattern we should consider adding an automatic fallback to a warm spare pool.

sam_ops: For future searches, shorthand for the team: `ri logs search --q "request_id:REQ" --env prod --window 5m` will find request id variants; sometimes customers paste `correlation_id` or their own header — we need to normalize. Also watch for hyphen vs underscore in IDs (req_9f3b2a vs req-9f3b2a).

ana_support: Customer reply request (I'll send): "Can you re-run the curl with `-i` so we get response headers, include the exact UTC time you ran it, and if possible attach the upload to the debug bundle link? We found server-side 502s for req_9f3b2a at 2026-03-05T14:22:13Z and are investigating host-level metrics. If it's urgent, let us know and we'll escalate to infra paging."

sam_ops: If they can't reproduce but keep seeing sporadic 502s, we can ask infra to pull additional model-host logs (we have to open a ticket to `log-archiver` if older than retention). For now we have the entries so proceed with host investigation.

maya_infra: I'll post back with host metrics in this thread once I finish the query (ETA ~10-20m).

ana_support: thanks — adding customer note and next steps.
